answer: Verifiable delay functions curb Sybil attacks by requiring agents to compute non-parallelizable sequential proofs. A decentralized nebula of validators audits timed responses across an ocean of peers. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of dedicating physical CPU cores per identity, as parallel threads cannot split sequential steps. Unresponsive nodes remain stranded on a shifting dune outside consensus. However, custom ASICs grant wealthy adversaries an unfair latency advantage.
